title: Forces and Motion
seo_title: Year 11 Science: Forces and Motion Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Scalar and vector quantities; contact and non-contact forces; gravity and weight; resultant forces; work done; forces and elasticity; speed, velocity and acceleration; distance–time and velocity–time graphs; Newton's laws; stopping distances; (higher tier) momentum and conservation of momentum.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on forces and motion: vectors and scalars, weight, resultant forces, Newton's laws, F = ma, F = ke, acceleration, stopping distances and momentum. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Forces change how objects move.

  • W = mg (g = 9.8 N/kg). F = ma. F = ke. p = mv.
  • Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time. v² − u² = 2as.
  • Stopping distance = thinking distance (reaction time) + braking distance (road, tyres, brakes).
Example

Resultant 20 N on 4 kg. Acceleration?

a = F ÷ m = 20 ÷ 4

Answer: 5 m/s²

Example

20 m/s, reaction time 0.7 s. Thinking distance?

20 × 0.7

Answer: 14 m

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mass (kg) and weight (N).
  • Thinking a moving object needs a resultant force to keep moving.
  • Thinking tiredness increases braking distance.

faq.a: The acceleration of an object is proportional to the resultant force and inversely proportional to its mass: F = ma.
Thinking distance depends on speed and reaction time (tiredness, alcohol, drugs, distractions). Braking distance depends on speed, the road, the tyres and the brakes.
Momentum = mass × velocity (p = mv). In a closed system, momentum before a collision equals momentum after.
